/-!
# Size Ramsey Number

This file defines the size Ramsey number for simple graphs.

## Definition

The size Ramsey number `r̂(G, H)` is the minimum number of edges in a graph `F`
such that any 2-coloring of `F`'s edges contains a copy of `G` in one color or `H` in the other.
-/

namespace SimpleGraph

/--
The size Ramsey number `r̂(G, H)` is the minimum number of edges in a graph `F`
such that any 2-coloring of `F`'s edges contains a copy of `G` in one color or `H` in the other.

A 2-coloring is represented by a subgraph `R ≤ F` (the "red" edges); the "blue" edges are `F \ R`.
-/
noncomputable def sizeRamsey {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    (G : SimpleGraph α) (H : SimpleGraph β) : ℕ :=
  sInf { m | ∃ (n : ℕ) (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
    F.edgeSet.ncard = m ∧
    ∀ (R : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), R ≤ F →
      G.IsContained R ∨ H.IsContained (F \ R) }

/--
A graph `G` is **Ramsey size linear** if there exists a constant `c > 0` such that
for all graphs `H` with `m` edges and no isolated vertices, `r̂(G, H) ≤ c · m`.
-/
def IsRamseySizeLinear {α : Type*} [Fintype α] (G : SimpleGraph α) : Prop :=
  ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (n : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel H.Adj],
    (∀ v, 0 < H.degree v) →
    (sizeRamsey G H : ℝ) ≤ c * H.edgeSet.ncard

end SimpleGraph

findings.description: Lines 55–58 define linear growth of the size Ramsey number r̂(G,H), which minimizes host edges. The standard notion 'Ramsey size linear' instead bounds the ordinary Ramsey number R(G,H), which minimizes host vertices. The docstring repeats this invariant swap. These predicates are not equivalent: K₃ is Ramsey size linear in the standard sense, but /workspace/review/Counterexample.lean proves that the current predicate fails for K₃. Specifically, it proves t² < 2 * sizeRamsey K₃ K₁,ₜ for every t > 0, ruling out a constant-times-t bound.
findings.source_evidence: Bradač–Gishboliner–Sudakov, arXiv:2202.10388v2, §1, first defines R(H,F) as the smallest N such that every graph on N vertices contains H or its complement contains F, and then defines Ramsey size-linearity by R(H,F) = O(e(F)) for every F without isolated vertices. The publisher abstract of Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp, 'Ramsey Size Linear Graphs', DOI 10.1017/S096354830000078X, gives the same definition and states that connected graphs with q ≤ p+1 are Ramsey size linear, including K₃.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep sizeRamsey unchanged: it correctly defines the size Ramsey number. Introduce an ordinary graph Ramsey number using `sInf {N : ℕ | ∀ R : SimpleGraph (Fin N), G.IsContained R ∨ H.IsContained Rᶜ}`, with the same finite-target assumptions. Use that number instead of `sizeRamsey G H` in IsRamseySizeLinear, and replace r̂ by R in its docstring.

findings.description: FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/566.lean, line 49, directly uses `sizeRamsey G H` where the source asks about the ordinary Ramsey number. This occurrence is independent of IsRamseySizeLinear, so fixing the shared predicate alone will not fix problem 566. The current right-hand side is false already for G = K₃: the triangle satisfies the exact induced-subgraph sparseness hypothesis, but its size Ramsey numbers against stars grow at least quadratically. Both facts, and the resulting refutation of this right-hand side, were proved in Counterexample.lean.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/566 states: 'Let G be such that any subgraph on k vertices has at most 2k−3 edges. Is it true that, if H has m edges and no isolated vertices, then R(G,H) ≪ m?' The linked original collection, https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~erdosproblems/erdos/newproblems/SizeRamseyLinear.html, likewise states `r(G,H) ≤ cn`, without a hat. BGS23, §1, explicitly identifies this as ordinary Ramsey size-linearity.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the conclusion by the corrected `IsRamseySizeLinear G`, or replace the explicit `sizeRamsey G H` with the ordinary graph Ramsey number. Correct the theorem docstring's r̂ notation as well. The existing sparseness hypothesis can remain unchanged.

The hypercube definition itself is correct; the mismatch is the Ramsey invariant used by the shared predicate.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/567 asks, for G equal to Q₃, K₃,₃, or H₅, whether `R(G,H) ≪ m` for every H with m edges and no isolated vertices. The original collection at https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~erdosproblems/erdos/newproblems/SizeRamseyLinearSpecific.html states `r(G,H) ≤ cn`. The ordinary meaning of R is explicit in arXiv:2202.10388v2, §1.

The original problem at https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~erdosproblems/erdos/newproblems/SizeRamseyLinearSpecific.html uses `r(G,H) ≤ cn`; arXiv:2202.10388v2, §1, defines this R as the ordinary Ramsey number.

findings.description: FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/567.lean, line 75, bounds size Ramsey numbers through the incorrect shared predicate instead of ordinary Ramsey numbers. This changes the question materially: the actual H5 definition contains a triangle, and Counterexample.lean proves `¬ Erdos567.H5.IsRamseySizeLinear` using the quadratic lower bound against stars. findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/567 asks whether `R(H₅,H) ≪ m` for arbitrary H without isolated vertices. Its remarks and arXiv:2202.10388v2, §1, distinguish the still-open general question from the proved ordinary-Ramsey bound when H is bipartite. Neither concerns the edge-minimizing size Ramsey number.
findings.suggested_fix: Repair IsRamseySizeLinear to use the ordinary Ramsey number; the theorem can retain its H5 argument. Correct the module docstring's r̂ notation. Do not change the problem's status on the basis of the refutation of the current, different formulation.

reformulations.difference: Binary edge-colourings are represented by spanning red subgraphs R ≤ F, with F \ R supplying the blue graph, rather than by functions from F's edges to two colours.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a Mathlib edge-labeling C : F.EdgeLabeling Bool, its true-labelled graph is a subgraph of F and its false-labelled graph equals F \ C.labelGraph true. Conversely, the characteristic function of R.edgeSet gives an edge-labeling whose true graph is R and whose false graph is F \ R. Consequently the two universally quantified monochromatic-copy conditions are equivalent. This exact iff was proved as Review.red_subgraph_iff_edgeLabeling in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

module

public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Copy
public import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
public import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card
public import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

@[expose] public section

/-!
# Ramsey Numbers and Ramsey Size Linearity

This file defines the size Ramsey number and ordinary Ramsey number for simple graphs,
and the notion of Ramsey size linearity.

## Definitions

The size Ramsey number `r̂(G, H)` is the minimum number of edges in a graph `F`
such that any 2-coloring of `F`'s edges contains a copy of `G` in one color or `H` in the other.
Ramsey size linearity instead bounds the ordinary Ramsey number `R(G, H)` linearly in the
number of edges of `H`.

## References

* Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp,
  [Ramsey size linear graphs](https://doi.org/10.1017/S096354830000078X).
-/

namespace SimpleGraph

/--
The size Ramsey number `r̂(G, H)` is the minimum number of edges in a graph `F`
such that any 2-coloring of `F`'s edges contains a copy of `G` in one color or `H` in the other.

A 2-coloring is represented by a subgraph `R ≤ F` (the "red" edges); the "blue" edges are `F \ R`.
-/
noncomputable def sizeRamsey {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    (G : SimpleGraph α) (H : SimpleGraph β) : ℕ :=
  sInf { m | ∃ (n : ℕ) (F : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
    F.edgeSet.ncard = m ∧
    ∀ (R : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), R ≤ F →
      G.IsContained R ∨ H.IsContained (F \ R) }

/--
The ordinary Ramsey number `R(G, H)` is the least number of vertices `n` such that any
red/blue coloring of the edges of the complete graph on `n` vertices contains a red copy of `G`
or a blue copy of `H`.

A coloring is represented by its red graph `R`; the blue graph is its complement `Rᶜ`.
-/
noncomputable def ramseyNumber {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    (G : SimpleGraph α) (H : SimpleGraph β) : ℕ :=
  sInf { n | ∀ R : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.IsContained R ∨ H.IsContained Rᶜ }

/--
A graph `G` is **Ramsey size linear** if there exists a constant `c > 0` such that
for all graphs `H` with `m` edges and no isolated vertices, the ordinary Ramsey number
satisfies `R(G, H) ≤ c · m`.
-/
def IsRamseySizeLinear {α : Type*} [Fintype α] (G : SimpleGraph α) : Prop :=
  ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (n : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel H.Adj],
    (∀ v, 0 < H.degree v) →
    (ramseyNumber G H : ℝ) ≤ c * H.edgeSet.ncard

end SimpleGraph
